observation.visible_scene: A close, slightly high-angle view of a rusty, soot-stained metal tabletop (a burner stand) with a large dull-metal pot resting on it and a single tubular leg visible at right over a concrete floor. From the left, a gloved hand holds a yellow-and-black handheld power tool whose working tip (a small spinning/oscillating brush-like end) is pressed against the tabletop along the front base of the pot. White smoke/steam rises continuously from the contact zone and drifts to the right, partially veiling the pot. Dark burnt patches and scattered grit/debris cover the surface.
visible_changes: The tool's tip traverses along the front edge of the pot's base from the left-centre of the frame toward the right over the clip (tip x-position shifts rightward from roughly mid-frame to the right side by the final frames).
The tool body/handle tilts and rotates as it moves, going from a steep down-left angle early to a more horizontal position crossing the top of the frame late.
The white smoke/steam plume fluctuates in density and shape, billowing more heavily through the middle-to-late frames while consistently rising and drifting right.
A small bright reflection/spark-like point appears intermittently at the working tip (e.g., early frames and several mid frames).
The green-gloved hand/arm at the lower left grows from a small corner presence into a large blurry mass occluding much of the left frame toward the end.
The metal tabletop under the tool shows progressively more of its lighter, scraped/cleaned patch as the tip passes, with the rusty edge remaining in front.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the smoke/steam (heat, steam, combustion, or chemical reaction) is not shown.
The exact function of the tool (cleaning, grinding, heating, etc.) and what happens before/after this segment are not visible.
Whether the pot is heated, and what is beneath it, is unknown.
uncertain_details: Whether the tip is a rotating wire brush, a nozzle, or another attachment is not certain from motion blur alone.
The slight shift of the pot and tool across the frame could be camera movement or tool movement; the right leg stays roughly fixed, suggesting the camera is mostly stable with minor shake.
The bright point at the tip may be a spark or a specular reflection; identity is unclear.
